$ cat testdata/checks/paths.txt
script evaluate: resolve's cell of script/x is built through parse, and the cell through parse2 past it
script evaluate: through resolve, parse2
script parse2: through no lift
script parse: through no lift
script resolve: through parse
$ go test  # ladder-a-paths
    the lift resolve is used by ./b on the path testdata/script/ → parse2 → resolve, and ., which owns it, runs it on the path testdata/script/ → parse → resolve, so no package writes the cells of resolve that ./b's cells past it are built through.
        A package that uses a lift reaches it from each corpus by the path the lift's owner does: either ./b reaches resolve from testdata/script/ by .'s path, or . by ./b's. Making a way true may need other registrations to change, such as a lift that would then close a cycle or give a type a second path. If they reach it alike already, a registry is stale: run FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./..., which rewrites the registry of every package with tests.
    what ran, in order:
        parse ran on x
        resolve ran on x
--- FAIL: TestCorpus
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/script
        --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/parse
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/resolve
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/checks
        --- PASS: TestCorpus/checks/paths
FAIL
[exit 1]

    testdata/script/x.txtar: no registry claims out/parse/outcome: no column named parse runs over the corpus script.
        If a column should write them, register the column. If not, run hypercase strip -root . -column parse at the module root. It removes parse's sections from every archive under the module-root corpus, but a frozen cell's, and lists what it leaves. Then run FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./... until it changes nothing, and read what it reports.
